summary: Observations of an orange luminous phenomenon in the sky towards Belgium.
description: Following a press article, the gendarmerie launched an investigation on October 1, 1975, into the observation by several witnesses of a large orange phenomenon seen in the distance in the sky over the towns of Elesnes-Assevent-Boussois and Vieux-Reng on Friday, September 26, 1975. The gendarmerie investigation identified two people with contradictory testimonies. Photographs taken by one of the witnesses and sent to the press proved negative. These individuals likely observed a phenomenon linked to the Charleroi metallurgical region in Belgium, which lies along the trajectory indicated by the witnesses. This case is classified as Class B.

summary: Successive observations of a scintillating phenomenon: astronomical misinterpretation.
description: Two witnesses observed, several nights in a row and under clear skies, a scintillating, circular phenomenon. Some observations were made with a telescope. Astronomical verification confirmed that, starting on February 17, 1975, a conjunction of Jupiter and Venus could be observed. These celestial bodies were gradually moving away from each other. The scintillation produced the rest of the effect observed with the telescope: apparent movement, color changes, etc. These witnesses made an astronomical error: the case is class A.

summary: Observation of vertical movements of a luminous phenomenon: lack of information.
description: On February 18, 1975, at approximately 12:20 a.m., a witness traveling on a country road was frightened by a luminous, spherical object that moved vertically and silently across the landscape. No other witness statements were collected. Astronomical verification indicated that the Moon was near setting in the west-northwest (azimuth 290), in the shape of a crescent moon (first quarter). The police report included a copy of the land registry map, which did not appear to be oriented with north at the top; the current version of the land registry map available through Geoportail (IGN) does not show the same orientation. Using the current reference map, the witness also observed the phenomenon in the west-northwest with an azimuth close to 287 (see attached map), that is, the direction of the Moon: confusion with the Moon, perhaps partially obscured to appear roughly spherical, is conceivable. Inaccurate estimation of distance and size is very common in UFO observations, especially for celestial bodies visible near the horizon. Nevertheless, with this hypothesis, it is difficult to explain the back-and-forth movements of the phenomenon described by the witness; one could perhaps consider that low clouds may have partially obscured the lunar half-disk. Since the witness does not mention the Moon, even though it was in the direction of their observation, it is highly probable that it played a role in the observation. In conclusion, lacking the ability to refine the apparent movements of the phenomenon with the witness and to verify the local atmospheric conditions, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" as an unidentifiable phenomenon due to a lack of precise data.

summary: Astronomical observations of a Venus-Jupiter conjunction.
description: On February 17, 1975, between 7:20 and 7:50 PM, several witnesses in different French departments observed the unusual presence of one or two large and particularly bright points in the sky. No noise was heard during the long observations made by the witnesses. These witnesses made an astronomical observation of the conjunction of the planets Venus and Jupiter, particularly visible at that time of year.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a circular and luminous object above the trees.
description: In September 1975, two people reported an observation made on February 15, 1975, around 6:00 PM: a luminous, circular object (about one meter in diameter) moved silently at a low altitude in the sky. It moved from east to west and disappeared behind trees. No other accounts or further details were gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of an object rotating on its own axis while moving.
description: Following press reports of an unidentified object being observed by several people on January 19, 1975, at 6:45 PM, the gendarmerie sought witnesses. Only two people were willing to testify, and only under the condition of anonymity. The object appeared to rotate on its axis and slowly move away toward the horizon on a downward trajectory before rapidly rising and disappearing. Another observation of the phenomenon was made on January 20, 1975, at the same time. Despite the consistency of the testimonies, this case is classified as Class C due to a lack of precise information.
